findings.title: Rejected device is cached as successfully tagged, bypassing the limit on retry
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device ID into localCache (29-minute TTL) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the caller denies authentication, but the cache entry remains, so the device's next request hits the cache at line 83, TagDevice returns nil, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants an identity even though the device was never recorded and the limit is still exceeded. A rejected client only has to retry once to bypass the device limit for the cache lifetime.

findings.title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert race
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts devices in one query and then performs the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert as a separate statement/session when count < deviceLimit. Concurrent requests (including from multiple Grafana instances sharing the database, where the per-instance local cache provides no coordination) can all observe count == limit-1 and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The limit needs an atomic/serialized enforcement (transaction with locking, unique-window constraint, or serialized writer), not a check-then-act across two sessions.

findings.title: Provider signature changed without regenerating Wire wiring
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed its second dependency from anonstore.AnonStore to db.DB, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a deviceLimit argument, but no wire_gen.go/wire set changes are included in this PR. The checked-in generated wiring still constructs and passes an *AnonDBStore where a db.DB is now expected and still calls ProvideAnonDBStore with one argument, so the server build/wire generation fails until the injector is regenerated and the now-redundant store provider binding is reconciled.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now synchronously performs DB writes and loses panic isolation
findings.body: Authenticate previously tagged devices in a background goroutine with a 2-minute detached-context timeout and a recover() for panics. It now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context: a slow/count-query-backed store blocks every anonymous authentication (cache misses add a COUNT plus INSERT/UPDATE round trip), request cancellation aborts tagging, and a panic in tagging propagates into the auth path instead of being logged. This turns device bookkeeping into a latency and availability dependency of anonymous login.

findings.title: New device_limit option is not declared in default/sample config or documentation
findings.body: The code reads [auth.anonymous] device_limit via MustInt64(0), but this PR adds no entry to conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini and no configuration documentation. Grafana convention declares every setting in defaults.ini (which also feeds config docs/overrides tooling); without it the new limit is undiscoverable for operators and omitted from generated config documentation, despite being the user-facing switch for this feature.
